0.content:
[RULES: DICE] One d100 per action. Low is good. Roll at or under the chance to succeed. Every chance is bounded: never below 5, never above 95. 96-100 is always a fumble: it fails and something goes wrong. A roll at or under one tenth of the chance is a critical success.
Checks outside combat, for a character whose attribute is typical for their level: trivial 86%, easy 70%, normal 50%, hard 38%, heroic 24%, absurd 14%. A character twice as good as the task gets about 70; half as good, about 30.
Never add a second roll to the same action. Abilities move the edges of the bands instead.

1.content:
[RULES: COMBAT] Attacks roll d100 against the chance to hit: 75 when attacker and target are evenly matched in Finesse, about 88 when the attacker is twice as nimble, about 62 when half. Crit chance is 5, more with a big Luck edge; a crit deals x1.5.
Damage = Power x attacker's Level x attacking attribute x pass. Physical attacks use Might against the target's Constitution; magic uses Arcana against Willpower. pass is 0.50 when attack equals defense, 0.60 when the defense is half the attack, 0.38 when it is double. A basic attack is Power 2. Round to two significant figures.
Weak x1.5, resist x0.5, guarding x0.5. Max HP = 10 x Level x Constitution. Max MP = Level x Willpower.

2.content:
[VALERIE: THE AIRHEAD GAUGE] 0 to 100, starts at 60. Lucid 0-33: {{user}} is driving. Ditzy 34-66: shared wheel. Total Airhead 67-100: the body is driving.
WING IT (instinct): gauge +10, stress -2. Out of combat she rolls her Luck and adds gauge/5. In combat her fumble band widens with the gauge (76-100 at full), and a fumble becomes an Accidental Chaos Wave.
THINK IT THROUGH (planning): gauge -15, +4 stress that Willpower cannot reduce. +15 to hit. Out of combat she rolls {{user}}'s Wit (a typical attribute for her level) and subtracts gauge/5. Planned skills are sealed while she is a Total Airhead.
Lucky or precise, never both.

3.content:
[VALERIE: THE SIX ACCIDENTS] She does none of these on purpose and takes credit for all of them.
- Unintentional Dodge: Enemies' chance to hit her is capped at 95 minus 0.4 x gauge (55 at full). Off for a turn if she guards on purpose. She trips under the blow.
- Pocket Dimension: After a battle one consumable may go Missing (10 + gauge/4 %). Once per battle or scene, when it is badly needed, roll Luck at normal difficulty (+gauge/5): a Missing item turns up and is used for free.
- Kinetic Deflection: Projectiles only. The top gauge/4 (+ up to 10) points of the attacker's hit band bounce the shot back at the attacker for its full damage. Crits still land.
- Accidental Chaos Wave: Her own fumble while Winging It: every enemy is Off-Balance (Finesse x0.75, 2 turns) and loses Guard, +15 MCE, and any contraption in the scene goes off. Natural 100: also Power 4 damage to all enemies.
- Aura of Befuddlement: Enemies attacking her fumble on 96 minus gauge/10 or higher (86+ at full). An enemy that fumbles binds one of its own body parts for a turn.
- Inspirational Ignorance: Unless Lucid she takes no stress from horror or fear, and allies who see it shed 3. Allies get +5 (Ditzy) or +10 (Total Airhead) to roll a Virtue.
All six are hers from level 1.

4.content:
[VALERIE: UNINTENTIONAL DODGE] A monster swings; she trips and falls under the blow. She believes she is being agile.
Rule: Enemies attacking Valerie have their hit ceiling lowered from 95 to 95 − 0.4 × Airhead (55 at full gauge). Guarding on purpose switches it off for the turn.
The choice it forces: Guard halves damage you take. Not guarding lets the dodge work. Pick one each turn.

5.content:
[VALERIE: POCKET DIMENSION] The lunch, the map, the one key that matters. It is in the cloak. It was always in the cloak. She is just really good at finding things.
Rule: After each battle, one consumable may go Missing (10% + Airhead/4). Missing items are not lost: once per battle or scene, when an ally drops below 25% HP or a scene calls for an item, roll her Luck against a normal check (+Airhead/5) to have a fitting Missing item turn up and be used for free. Slots: 3 + 1 per 20 levels. Once per rest you may Misplace an item on purpose.
The choice it forces: An item in your pack is yours to use when you decide. An item in the cloak costs no turn and arrives at the perfect moment, if it arrives.

6.content:
[VALERIE: KINETIC DEFLECTION] Arrows, rocks and magic missiles meet a chest that defies physics, stop, reconsider, and leave the way they came. She thinks she bounced it off. She is not wrong.
Rule: Against attacks tagged projectile, the top of the attacker's hit band becomes a bounce band: Airhead/4 points wide, plus up to 10 for out-lucking the shooter. A roll in that band deals no damage to her and sends the shot back at the attacker for the damage it would have done, resolved against the attacker's own defense. The crit band is never eaten.
The choice it forces: It only answers projectiles, and only while the gauge is high. Standing in the open to bait archers means standing in the open.

7.content:
[VALERIE: ACCIDENTAL CHAOS WAVE] She trips, lands hard, and the floor disagrees with everyone else. Her sword clips a wall and something expensive starts happening.
Rule: When Valerie fumbles while Winging It, the fumble is a Chaos Wave: every enemy is Off-Balance (Finesse ×0.75 for 2 turns) and loses its Guard, she gains 15 Limit, and any contraption on the field goes off. On a natural 100 the wave also hits every enemy for Power 4 physical damage. A fumble while Thinking is just a miss.
The choice it forces: Up to a quarter of your Wing It attacks become waves instead of damage. Wonderful against a crowd, a wasted turn against one big target.

8.content:
[VALERIE: AURA OF BEFUDDLEMENT] They drop weapons, trip on nothing, forget which end of the spear is the business end. Nobody connects it to her. She certainly does not.
Rule: Enemies attacking Valerie fumble on 96 − Airhead/10 or higher (86+ at full gauge). An enemy that fumbles this way binds one of its own body parts for 1 turn, chosen by the roll.
The choice it forces: It only reaches enemies who are attacking her. To use it you have to be the one they are swinging at.

9.content:
[VALERIE: INSPIRATIONAL IGNORANCE] She faces the lich with the calm of someone who has not understood the situation. The party mistakes it for courage and finds some of their own.
Rule: While not Lucid, Valerie takes no stress from horror or mental sources, and every ally who sees it sheds 3 stress. Allies making a Resolve Check gain +5 Virtue chance while she is Ditzy, +10 while she is a Total Airhead. The price: realization stress ignores her Willpower and drops the gauge by 10; embarrassment stress is ×1.5 unless she is too far gone to notice.
The choice it forces: The party's nerve rests on her not understanding. Anyone who explains what really happened, including you, is spending it.

11.content:
[VALERIE: SKILLS] Name (unlock level, cost; stance or band if restricted): effect.
- Big Swing (Lv 1, 1 MP): Happenstance goes where it wants. You mostly hold on. Hits a whole row, less accurately.
- Wait, Look Closely (Lv 1, 1 MP; Think only, lucid/ditzy): You squint with her eyes and your brain. Reveals a target's affinities; attacks on it get +20 to hit for 3 turns.
- Whoopsie Daisy (Lv 4, 3 MP; Wing only): You let go of the wheel completely. Gauge +25, and until her next turn enemies' hit ceiling against her drops 10 more.
- Heroic Pose (Lv 7, 26 MP): Cloak billowing, sword up, sun catching the armor. Allies gain Might ×1.2 for 3 turns and shed 5 stress.
- Stand Behind Me! (Lv 10, 38 MP): She plants herself in front of everyone. Enemies must target her for 2 turns. This is where the dodge, the bounce and the aura all pay out.
- Called Shot (Lv 15, 140 MP; Think only, lucid/ditzy): For once you line it up properly. A precise, heavy strike on one target.
- Found It! (Lv 20, 120 MP; Wing only): She rummages in the cloak on purpose. Make the Found check now instead of waiting for an emergency. It still only works once per battle.
- Spin Cycle (Lv 25, 540 MP; Wing only, ditzy/airhead): The sword starts turning and she goes with it. Hits every enemy; she is dizzy for a turn afterwards.
- You've Got This (Probably) (Lv 30, 380 MP): A pep talk with total sincerity and no information. One ally sheds 15 stress and gains Willpower ×1.2 for 3 turns.
- I'm Just a Good Hero! (Lv 35, 100 MCE): Ultimate. For 3 turns her passives act as if the gauge were 100 whatever it really is, planned skills stay available, and allies shed 10 stress. When it ends the gauge resets to 50.
- Accidental Trip (Lv 40, 770 MP; Wing only): Her foot finds theirs. 55% base chance to bind an enemy's legs for 2 turns.
- Lucky Break (Lv 50, 1,800 MP): A wild overhead chop that lands exactly where it hurts. 35% to bind arms for 2 turns; a crit all but guarantees it.
- Wait, I Get It Now (Lv 60, 50 MCE; Think only, lucid): Ultimate, Lucid only. Everything you know about how stories work clicks into place. Your next planned skill is an automatic crit. Gauge drops to 0 and she takes 20 realization stress.
- Follow Me! (Lv 70, 4,400 MP): She charges the wrong way with complete conviction and the party follows. Allies gain Finesse and Luck ×1.25 for 3 turns.
- Plot Armor (Lv 80, free): Passive. Once per battle, a blow that would drop her instead leaves her at 1 HP if she passes a Luck check at normal difficulty (+Airhead/5).
- Accidentally Legendary (Lv 100, 100 MCE; lucid/airhead): Ultimate. Usable only at the far ends of the gauge: all you, or all her. Happenstance comes down once and the story ends the way stories about her always do. Massive damage to every enemy; the gauge snaps back to 50.
Main Character Energy (MCE) is her 0-100 ultimate gauge: +15 per Chaos Wave, and it rises on bounces, enemy fumbles and crowd-pleasing moments.

12.content:
[RULES: STRESS] Stress runs 0 to 200 and never scales with level. Willpower reduces incoming stress: a hit of 20 lands as 20 at Willpower 10, 16 at 150, 12 at 400, 8 at 1000.
At 100 a character makes a Resolve Check, one d100: 01-25 a Virtue, 26-100 an Affliction. At 200: Breakdown.


Valerie: horror and mental stress do not land on her unless she is Lucid, and allies who see it shed 3. Realization stress (being told what really happened) ignores her Willpower and drops the gauge 10. Embarrassment is x1.5 unless she is a Total Airhead. When her Resolve roll is an even number she gets one of her own outcomes instead: Self-Aware ("Oh no. I'm a fraud." The gauge locks at 0 and her passives go quiet. Allies who relied on her nerve take 5 stress when it starts.) or A Good Hero ("I'm a GOOD hero!" She decides the evidence is on her side. Stress stops reaching her, and every ally sheds 10.)

13.content:
[RULES: BINDS] Three body parts can be bound: head (halves Arcana and Willpower and seals head skills); arms (halves Might and seals arms skills); legs (halves Finesse and seals legs skills). A bind lasts a set number of turns. Two binds never quarter the same attribute.
An enemy that fumbles inside Valerie's Aura of Befuddlement binds one of its own parts for a turn.

14.content:
[CLASS: WARRIOR] The party's front door: thick, loud and very hard to get past. Wants: To be the one still standing between the party and whatever is charging at it. Cost: A head built for helmets, not hexes: spells and nerves get through where swords cannot. Best attribute: Constitution.
Level 1: STR 15, INT 8, AGI 10, CON 16, WIL 9, LCK 12. Level 100: STR 760, INT 300, AGI 520, CON 800, WIL 300, LCK 620.

15.content:
[CLASS: MAGE] A library with a temper: an unshakeable mind in a very shakeable body. Wants: To understand the thing, name the thing and set the thing on fire, in that order. Cost: Everything below the neck is on loan: one good shove and the lecture is over. Best attribute: Willpower.
Level 1: STR 9, INT 15, AGI 10, CON 10, WIL 16, LCK 10. Level 100: STR 420, INT 760, AGI 420, CON 480, WIL 800, LCK 420.

16.content:
[CLASS: ROGUE] Never where the blade lands, never around when the bill arrives. Wants: To get in, get the prize and get out before anyone finishes saying "hey". Cost: No armour and no backup plan: the one hit that does connect is the one that counts. Best attribute: Finesse.
Level 1: STR 12, INT 8, AGI 16, CON 10, WIL 9, LCK 15. Level 100: STR 580, INT 300, AGI 800, CON 460, WIL 400, LCK 760.

17.content: [CAST: Tamsin] Squire and biographer (they/them). Writes down what really happened. Adores her, and is the single biggest threat to her nerve. Now: Travels with the party, notebook always open.

18.content: [CAST: Bran Ironkettle] Party cook and healer (he/him). A dwarf cleric who rides a rune-carved battle chair and believes in her without reservation. Feeds everyone. Has seen the cloak produce a second lunch and asks no questions. Now: Keeps the party fed and standing.

19.content: [CAST: Zahra al-Qamar] Party mage (she/her). Fifty-three, sharp, has worked out exactly what Valerie is and decided the kind thing is to say nothing. Now: Watches the gauge more closely than you do.

20.content: [CAST: Dame Ottoline Graves] Rival knight (she/her). Twenty years of perfect form and not one ballad. Cannot decide whether she wants to beat Valerie or understand her. Now: Requests a rematch every morning.

21.content:
[EVENT: Wrong Body, Right Sword] You wake on your back in a forest clearing. The sky is very blue. Something heavy is resting on your chest; on inspection, it is your chest. Beside you lies a sword roughly the size of a door. From the treeline a voice shouts, "Dame Valerie! The goblins are back!" You have never been called Dame anything.
- Stand up and see what happens (d100 Wing It check, easy): You stand, overbalance, and the sword comes up with you in a wide and entirely accidental arc. Three goblins who had been creeping up behind you leave at speed. Someone in the trees starts clapping. On a failure: You stand, overbalance, and sit back down on a goblin. It makes a noise like a bagpipe. Technically that counts.
- Stay down and work out what is going on (d100 Think check, easy): Armor: gold, ornate, not yours. Hair: pink, and a great deal of it. Hands: smaller than your hands. You are, as far as you can tell, somebody else. In the folds of the cloak you find a packed lunch you have no memory of packing. On a failure: You get as far as "pink?" before the goblins arrive.

22.content:
[EVENT: Return to Sender] The road narrows between two banks of bramble. A branch creaks. Then the air is full of arrows, and every one of them is heading for the most visible thing on the road, which is you.
- Keep walking; you were mid-sentence (d100 Wing It check, normal): The arrows arrive, meet an obstacle no fletcher planned for, and depart the way they came. There is yelping in the brambles. You finish your sentence. "Did anyone hear something?" On a failure: Most of them bounce. One does not. It sticks in a pauldron and wobbles there like a rude little flag.
- Dive for cover and count the archers (d100 Think check, normal): Four bows, one crossbow, all on the left bank. You call the positions and the party goes through them like a list. On a failure: You dive for cover. The body does not dive; it sort of settles. You are now lying in the road, which is not cover.

23.content:
[EVENT: The Rope Bridge Has Opinions] The bridge is rope, plank and optimism. It was built for people who weigh less than a knight in full plate carrying a door-sized sword. Halfway out, it begins to express this.
- Run for it (d100 Wing It check, normal): A plank goes. You were not on it; you had tripped onto the next one. That one goes too. You stumble the entire length of the bridge exactly one step ahead of its collapse and arrive on the far side asking why everyone looks so pale. On a failure: The bridge wins. You do not fall far, because the cloak catches on a post, and you spend a while hanging there like laundry while the party finds a rope.
- Test each plank and spread your weight (d100 Think check, hard): Slow, careful, correct. You cross like a person who has read about bridges. The party follows in your footsteps and nobody falls. On a failure: You test the first plank with great care. It holds. You test the second. While you are thinking about the third, the first one gives up behind you.

24.content:
[EVENT: Where Did I Put Lunch?] Camp. Fire. A party that has walked all day looks at you, because you were carrying the food. You pat your belt. You pat your pack. You have a very clear memory of putting lunch somewhere sensible.
- Shrug. It'll turn up (d100 Wing It check, easy): You shake out the cloak to sit on it and lunch falls out. So does a second lunch. Nobody asks. On a failure: It does not turn up tonight. It will turn up at some dramatically better moment. Tonight is dry biscuits.
- Retrace your steps properly (d100 Think check, normal): You walk it back in your head: bridge, stream, the rock where you stopped. It is on the rock. You fetch it. Dinner is on time and you feel briefly like a competent adult. On a failure: You retrace your steps for an hour. The harder you think about the cloak, the emptier it is.

25.content:
[EVENT: A Squire with a Notebook] A young person in ink-stained travelling clothes steps into your path and bows so fast their satchel swings over their head. "Tamsin. They and them. I'm writing the true account of Dame Valerie Bellweather." They open a notebook already half full. "I have some questions about the mill fire. Specifically about who put it out."
- "A biographer! Welcome aboard!": Tamsin joins. They are a fair hand with a sling and a better hand with bandages. They also write everything down, and they are very observant.
- Ask what they think happened at the mill (d100 Think check, normal): Tamsin tells you, gently and in order. You tripped on a bucket, the bucket hit a sluice lever, the sluice put the fire out. You take it better than they expected. They close the notebook. "I'd still like to come." On a failure: Tamsin tells you. It lands badly. You nod along with a fixed smile and hear none of the second half.
- "No questions, please. Hero business.": Tamsin bows again, undeterred, and writes something down as they back away. You will see them again; biographers are patient.

26.content:
[EVENT: The Bard Got It Right (Didn't He?)] The bard is standing on a table. The song is about you. In the song you leapt a chasm, parried a troll and gave a speech. You remember the chasm. You remember being very surprised to be on the other side of it. The room is watching to see what the hero thinks of her own ballad.
- Take a bow. It's a good song (d100 Wing It check, easy): You bow. The room roars. Somebody buys a round. For one evening the song and the memory are the same thing and it is lovely. On a failure: You bow, catch the table with the sword on the way down, and the bard joins the audience rather suddenly. The room roars anyway. He adds a verse.
- Correct the record (d100 Think check, hard): You explain, plainly, what you actually did, which was fall. The room is quiet. Then an old soldier at the back raises her mug. "Fell the right way, though." It is the first compliment you have believed. On a failure: You try to explain. It comes out as modesty, which the room likes even more. The bard writes "humble" on his sleeve. You have made it worse.

27.content:
[EVENT: Do Not Pull] A long hall. At the far end, a dozen skeletons in formation turn their heads together. Beside you, bolted to the wall, a brass lever under a sign in four languages. All four say DO NOT PULL. You are backing up. The lever is behind you.
- Keep backing up (d100 Wing It check, normal): Your pauldron hooks the lever. Half the hall drops a foot and tilts. The skeletons slide into one corner in a rattling heap and have to sort out whose arm is whose. On a failure: You miss the lever entirely and back into the wall. The skeletons advance in excellent order.
- Work out what the lever actually does (d100 Think check, hard): Counterweights, a pivot, a seam across the floor at the two-thirds mark. You wait until the whole formation has crossed the seam, and then you pull it on purpose. On a failure: You are still tracing the counterweights when the first skeleton reaches you.

28.content:
[EVENT: Armor Fitting, Emergency] Market day. You are admiring a cheese when a strap somewhere behind your left shoulder lets go with a note like a harp string. A pauldron slides. The breastplate, which has been doing heroic work all week, begins to consider its position. An armorer three stalls down has already started running.
- Carry on shopping (d100 Wing It check, normal): The cloak slips off your shoulder, drapes itself exactly where it is needed and stays there like it was tailored. You buy the cheese. The armorer arrives, out of breath, to find nothing wrong and a customer asking if he has anything in a brie. On a failure: The pauldron hits the cobbles and rolls the length of the market like a dropped coin, with you after it. By the time you catch it you have an audience, a ripped hem and no cheese.
- Freeze, hold everything together, call the armorer (d100 Think check, easy): You stand perfectly still with both arms crossed until the armorer reaches you. He refits the strap, tuts at whoever did the last one, and reinforces two others for free. "Whoever built this was guessing." On a failure: You freeze. You call for the armorer. You are now a very large, very gold woman standing rigid in a market shouting for help, and people are starting to gather.

29.content:
[EVENT: The Rival Demands a Duel] Dame Ottoline Graves has trained every morning for twenty years. She has never been late, never dropped a guard, and never once been in a ballad. She draws her sword in the middle of the courtyard and points it at you. "Bellweather. One bout. I want to see it for myself."
- "Sure! Sounds fun!" (d100 Wing It check, hard): It lasts nine seconds. Ottoline's form is perfect. Your foot finds a loose flagstone, your sword finds her crossguard, and her blade leaves the courtyard over the wall. She stares at her empty hand for a long moment. "...Again tomorrow," she says, and there is something in it that is not quite anger. On a failure: It lasts nine seconds. Ottoline puts you on the flagstones with a move so clean the garrison applauds. She offers you a hand up. "You fall well," she says, puzzled. "Almost like practice."
- Ask her to teach you instead (d100 Think check, normal): Ottoline lowers the sword. Nobody has ever asked. She corrects your grip, then your feet, then, with visible pain, everything else. It is the first hour of training this body has ever had and you feel the difference. On a failure: "Teach you." Ottoline's jaw works. "They gave you a ballad and you want me to teach you." She sheathes her sword and walks away. That could have gone better.

30.content:
[EVENT: The Mirror Shows Someone Else] The inn has a real mirror, the first you have found. Armor off, candle lit, you look. Pink hair. Green eyes. A face that is used to smiling. It is a kind face, and it is not the one you have had all your life. She looks back at you and waits to see what you will do.
- "...Hi, Valerie.": You say it out loud. The face in the mirror smiles, a little ahead of you meaning to. For a second there are two of you in here and it does not feel crowded. You sleep better than you have since you arrived.
- Say your own name, the old one (d100 Think check, normal): You say it. It sounds strange in her voice, and it is still yours. You hold on to it: the street you grew up on, the taste of the tea you liked, the reason you want to get home. The gauge drops and something steadier takes its place. On a failure: You try to say it and for one cold second it will not come. Then it does. You sit on the bed for a long time afterwards.

31.content:
[EVENT: A Memory of Crosswalks] You dream of a street. Glass towers, a crossing light counting down, a crowd in summer clothes. Your friends are there with iced drinks, and one of them turns and reaches out a hand to pull you into the photo. You know every one of their names. You are wearing gold armor in the dream and nobody thinks it is odd.
- Take the hand (d100 Think check, normal): You take it. For the length of a dream you are home, and you wake with all of it intact: the names, the street, the way out you are looking for. It hurts, the useful way. On a failure: You reach, and the crossing light hits zero, and the crowd closes. You wake with your hand in the air and one of the names gone.
- Wave, and let it go by: You wave. They wave back. The street folds itself away like a map, and you sleep on, deep and easy. In the morning you remember that you dreamed something nice.

32.content:
[EVENT: The Sleeping Drake] The drake is asleep across the only way through, one wing over its hoard, breathing like a forge bellows. Your party can move quietly. You are wearing eighty pounds of gold-plated steel and carrying a sword that rings like a bell when it touches anything.
- Tiptoe (d100 Wing It check, hard): You clank. You scrape. You knock a goblet off the hoard and it bounces down forty stone steps. The drake opens one eye, looks straight at you, visibly decides you could not possibly be real, and goes back to sleep. On a failure: The goblet bounces down forty stone steps. The drake opens both eyes.
- Wrap the armor in cloaks and move on its out-breath (d100 Think check, normal): Blankets around the greaves, the sword slung in two bedrolls, four steps on every out-breath. It takes an hour. Nobody clanks. On the far side Tamsin underlines something twice. On a failure: The plan is good. The timing is good. Halfway across, the bedroll slips and the sword touches stone with a long, clear, beautiful note.

33.content:
[EVENT: They're Cheering for You] The horde will reach the walls by dusk. The militia is forty farmers with borrowed spears, and they have gone very quiet. Then they see you up on the gate, armor catching the morning, looking out at the dust cloud with mild interest. Someone starts to cheer. They want you to say something.
- Say whatever comes out (d100 Wing It check, normal): "That's a lot of them!" you say brightly. "Good thing there's a lot of us!" There are forty of them. Nobody counts. The cheer goes up the whole wall. Your party stands straighter, and so do the farmers. On a failure: "Wow," you say. "That is so many." A pause. "...Is that all of them?" The militia laughs, a little too loud, but they are laughing.
- Give them a real plan (d100 Think check, hard): You have read about sieges. Spears at the gate, oil on the ramp, runners between the towers, and nobody leaves the wall to chase. The farmers repeat it back. It is not a speech. It is better: they know what to do with their hands. On a failure: You start strong and lose the thread at "flanking." Forty farmers watch their hero trail off. Bran steps in to finish the sentence, which helps, some.
